items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: The transcript mentions 'John Bunce' in a parenthetical note by the interviewer/narrator, but the interviewee (Wilbur B. Ware, Sr) does not mention John Bunce in his spoken response, nor does he describe any personal interaction or relationship with him.

ctx.x: There was a certain amount of temperament going on. the union

and John Bunce; in fact, Buddy and I did call me up to do a commercial for Alcoa Aluminum, just bass and drums, and I don't know whether that was the end results, but I got paid for it, and then we had -- we got the Cork and Bob out in (unintelligible) at Westbury, Long Island, and I had worked out there before; I worked with my own little trio, and had worked with some other people, and tried to ... a fellow named Charlie Graziano who owned the place -- jazz buff.

And this particular night, the place was just jammed because you know, I told you, I played drums occasionally, and we were playing and I'm standing right behind Buddy, and when we finished, [unintelligible] I took the subway over and Buddy got up from his set and was bounding toward me with his sticks in his hand, you know, and somebody in the crowd hollered, "Play some drums, Wilbur" and I thought Buddy was offering me the sticks, so I got the sticks out of his hand, and slid in the seat and looked over to the…
